name: Modular monolith with an asynchronous triage worker
summary: One codebase and one deployable artifact, run as two process types: the HTTP service and the worker. One database; each module owns its tables. Triage runs from a durable queue table, so no request waits for the model.

components.name: Browsers, API clients and the support inbox
relay.worker: triage worker (later also the escalation evaluator)
Relay database: tasks, rules, triage_jobs; tables owned by modules

flows.data: ticket text out; suggested labels back
escalation emails: link, priority, rule, step; never the title

ESC-N01: The worker writes suggestions to its own table and never touches a task; one fitness test checks that no module but the service reaches the worker, and code review sees every path in one repository.
ESC-N03: One permission module (relay.roles) and one audit table serve every route; the 400-day retention is one setting on one database.
ESC-N04: The cap counts emails per target across all rules; with one database the count and the send are in one transaction.
ESC-N05: Target validation lives in one module; either option can do it.
ESC-N06: A rule change and its notification are written in one transaction; the worker sends it.
ESC-N07: Task titles never leave the process except as a link; one place to test.
ESC-N09: One worker heartbeat and one queue to watch; the 5-minute stall flag is in /healthz.
ESC-N10: Calls only email and webhook delivery; no new paid service.
CON-1: One artifact, one pipeline, one database and one set of dashboards for one rota.
CON-2: One artifact on the daily train; a change across modules ships as one change.
CON-3: The limiter is in the service; exact for one process, needs shared storage for several (a recorded consequence).
CON-4: POST /v1/triage-jobs inserts a row and returns 202; the model is called by the worker.
CON-5: Webhook sends are jobs with idempotency keys; receivers get the same delivery ID twice.
CON-6: Worker processes scale separately from web processes, from the same artifact.
